agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: The bill adds a competitive HRSA grant program in the Public Health Service Act for AI education and training of medical students, residents and faculty at qualified medical schools and residency sponsoring institutions. It authorizes $1,000,000 per fiscal year for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
summary.long: The bill amends Part C of title VII of the Public Health Service Act by adding subpart III (Secs. 749C to 749G). The Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Health Resources and Services Administration, must establish a competitive grant program for qualified medical schools or residency sponsoring institutions to educate and train medical students, medical residents and medical faculty in deploying artificial intelligence in the medical profession. Individual grants may not exceed $100,000, and a recipient may receive no more than $100,000 per fiscal year. Permitted uses include AI for diagnostics and treatment recommendations, integration into clinical decision-making, instruction on ethical issues such as bias and patient data privacy, and practical demonstrations. Administrative costs are capped at 10 percent, and grant funds may not support publication in predatory journals. Recipients must submit annual reports starting within 180 days of receiving a grant, and must make funded educational materials publicly available within 30 days of each report. The Secretary gives priority to schools serving medically underserved communities and may award no more than two grants within the same 2020 Census Division. The authorization of $1,000,000 per fiscal year covers fiscal years 2026 through 2030.](placeholder)
